title: Tata Communications Ltd - 500483 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Tata Communications Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 21.2% Y-o-Y to ₹1,422 crore, with digital portfolio EBITDA margin at -3.6%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 9.6% Y-o-Y to ₹6,688 crore and EBITDA rose 21.2% to ₹1,422 crore, with EBITDA margin at 21.3%. Management attributed the profit improvement mainly to a sharp cut in digital portfolio losses, which fell from -6.9% margin in Q1 to -3.6% in Q2. Data revenue grew 12.2% reported but only about 6% after normalising for a stronger dollar, and management said order book grew double digits. PAT after minorities rose 86% to ₹341 crore, FCF turned positive at ₹212 crore, and an in-principle settlement was reached with the Canada Revenue Agency on a tax matter.

financial_highlights.change: +12.2% Y-o-Y reported; about +6% Y-o-Y normalised for currency
Healthy double-digit growth at constant currency
+21.2% Y-o-Y; H1 EBITDA +14.8% Y-o-Y (management also cited ~15% in H1)
Sharp improvement from negative FCF in Q1

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA to operating cash flow conversion

financial_highlights.change: Net debt/EBITDA 2.17x, steady despite dividend payment

segments.name: Digital portfolio
segments.commentary: Revenue up 18.6% Y-o-Y, led by interaction (CIS/Commotion), next-gen connectivity and IoT; EBITDA margin improved to -3.6% from -6.9% in Q1, described as close to breakeven.

segments.name: Next-gen connectivity
segments.commentary: Growing about 27% Y-o-Y per management, with MCC Flex (multi-cloud connect) and dynamic DC-to-DC connectivity cited as drivers.

segments.name: Media
segments.commentary: Management said media improved in profitability and Q-o-Q revenue rose, but Y-o-Y growth remained soft; cost initiatives under way and LA Olympics support expected next year. A Middle East event was cancelled.

segments.name: Cloud
segments.commentary: Revenue growth muted; management is shifting toward selling own AI and sovereign cloud on owned GPUs rather than third-party distribution, which it said is margin-accretive. India cloud order book strong.

segments.name: Interaction / CIS
segments.commentary: Being run with Commotion as one P&L; Voice AI deployments live at HDFC ERGO and a win at Tata Consumer (Sales Saathi). Management did not disclose client count.

guidance_outlook: Management committed to double-digit EBITDA growth for FY27 and to turn the digital portfolio EBITDA positive as soon as possible.
Order book grew double digits Y-o-Y in Q2 and management expects it to convert into revenue; said Q2 was the best order-book quarter so far, with no large single wins.

Management expects higher-profit recurring revenue mix (platform, infrastructure, services and solutions) and said the investor call in February will outline longer-term growth and medium-term targets.
Management said the Q2 margin level, including implied core connectivity margin of about 44.8%, is achievable in coming quarters with no one-offs.
Media cost optimisation benefits expected to play out over coming quarters.
capex_capacity: Cash capex trended up in Q2, driven by undersea cable assets and DC-to-DC network expansion; management stressed capital efficiency and anchor-customer-led expansion.
Network footprint cited: over 80,000 km terrestrial fibre in India, 30,000 km metro fibre, and connectivity across 118 data centres.
GPU capacity bought and invested in is to be utilised through own sovereign/AI cloud products.
Management said it will scale capacity in line with customer demand rather than ahead of it.
demand_pricing: Order book robust, double-digit Y-o-Y growth, spread across regions and segments; some wins came against strong credible competition.
Neo-cloud multi-million dollar engagement for multi-terabyte connectivity linking CPU clusters for AI data-centre build-out in India.
Commotion AI model is SaaS-style: platform fee plus consumption charges for voice minutes, network and GPU usage; pricing varies by solution.
Constant-currency focus: management said EBITDA grew about 10% Y-o-Y at constant currency in H1.
Management projects 70 petabytes of data-centre traffic by 2036 versus about 2-3 petabytes now (as stated).

qa_highlights.question: When will constant-currency data growth reach double digits given strong order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said order book converts to revenue as implemented, expects Q2 to be the best order-book quarter so far, and asked analysts to wait one more quarter for core connectivity demand to show up in revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the digital margin expansion driven by mix, given rising collaboration/CPaaS share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main driver is a change in sales contribution margin, with rising platform revenue (AI-led wins, recurring, SaaS-like) lifting NR-to-GR ratio.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cloud business muted growth a deliberate shift to own-platform, higher-margin revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the focus is on selling own AI and sovereign cloud on owned GPUs across channels, trading off third-party distribution revenue for margin.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term digital margin targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no target; said the goal is EBITDA positive as soon as possible and details will come at the Investor Day, with a platform, solutions and infrastructure mix to balance capital intensity.

qa_highlights.question: How does Commotion monetise and how many clients use it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose client numbers; model is platform fee plus consumables, with revenue flowing back to individual towers.

risks_watch: Data revenue growth of about 6% at constant currency versus 12.2% reported; FX headwind from stronger dollar.
Commotion and AI revenue not separately disclosed; client count withheld.
Media revenue soft Y-o-Y and event-driven; Middle East event cancellations.
Canada Revenue Agency settlement terms still being finalised; contingent liability of ₹1,658 crore as of 31 March 2026.
Cloud revenue muted as company shifts to own-platform sales; order-book conversion timing for network business uncertain.
Digital portfolio still EBITDA negative at -3.6%.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability, order book and AI positioning, but evasive on numbers: management withheld Commotion client counts, medium-term margin targets and AI revenue share, deferring these to the February Investor Day.
key_quotes: And my single largest focus in the last six months has been profitable growth.
Our losses have become less than half of what was in Q1. With this, we are very close to EBITDA breakeven for the overall digital portfolio.
Our focus is going to be constant currency growth.
Tata Comm has always had the stack. We have built the stack with our acquisition, with our GPUs investments.

adds.what: Undersea cable assets and DC-to-DC network expansion (cash capex trended up; no specific capacity count disclosed)

growth.why: Management reiterated double-digit EBITDA growth for FY27 (no revenue guidance given), backed by a double-digit order book increase and margin recovery from digital portfolio cost cuts, while cash capex rose for undersea cable and DC-to-DC expansion; backing is partial since no specific order values, capacity counts or timelines were quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Digital portfolio EBITDA margin improved to -3.6% from -6.9% in Q1, management says Q2 margin level incl. ~44.8% core connectivity margin is achievable in coming quarters, and FY27 EBITDA guided up double digits (H1 EBITDA +14.8% Y-o-Y).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Undersea cable and DC-to-DC network expansion is under way with cash capex trending up, but no capacity count or dated commissioning was disclosed and management will scale in line with customer demand.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book grew double digits Y-o-Y and Q2 was the best order-book quarter so far, but constant-currency data revenue growth is only about 6% and management asked analysts to wait one more quarter for core connectivity demand to show in revenue.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation not disclosed, and management is deferring medium-term targets and capital plans to the February investor call, with GPU capacity to be deployed through own sovereign/AI cloud.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held only the double-digit FY27 EBITDA growth target and gave no revenue guidance, with constant-currency data growth near 6%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Data revenue is about 6% constant-currency versus 12.2% reported, media growth is soft with a Middle East event cancelled, and cloud revenue is muted by the shift away from third-party distribution.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Own AI and sovereign cloud on owned GPUs is being pushed across channels, and Commotion Voice AI is live at HDFC ERGO with a Tata Consumer win, though no product dates were given.

rows.label: Digital portfolio to EBITDA positive
rows.why: Digital margin moved from -6.9% in Q1 to -3.6% in Q2 and management aims to turn EBITDA positive 'at the soonest', but gave no date and the margin is still negative.

rows.label: Media cost optimisation
rows.why: Media profitability improved and Q-o-Q revenue rose, with cost initiatives under way and LA Olympics support expected next year, though Y-o-Y growth remains soft.

rows.label: Positive free cash flow
rows.why: FCF turned positive at ₹212 crore from negative in Q1 and EBITDA-to-operating-cash conversion was 72%, but cash capex is rising for undersea cable and DC-to-DC expansion.

tone.note: Management was confident on the digital margin recovery, double-digit order book and AI positioning, but evasive on Commotion client counts, AI revenue share and medium-term margin targets, deferring these to February; analysts pushed on when constant-currency data growth reaches double digits.

oneOffs.what: Reported data revenue growth of 12.2% vs about 6% normalised for a stronger dollar; FX translation adds roughly 6 points to the headline data growth

quality.why: Consolidated revenue grew 9.6% and data revenue 12.2% reported, but only about 6% at constant currency, so roughly half of the data growth is currency translation rather than the recurring business; the EBITDA jump of 21.2% is mainly a cut in digital-portfolio losses (margin -6.9% to -3.6%) and PAT growth of 86% is not explained by the brief, which also mentions a Canada tax settlement with no amo
